title: p0011
universal_lens: The fusion of inertial dead-reckoning and optical trilateration forms a hybrid state-space estimator. By coupling high-frequency local kinematics with sparse global geometric constraints, the system minimizes cumulative drift while overcoming line-of-sight occlusions, yielding a robust continuous manifold for dynamic spatial tracking.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal Bayesian inference to map inertial sensor noise against optical ground truth. The position aiding acts as a periodic prior update, dynamically recalibrating posterior distributions of athlete trajectories, thereby quantifying epistemic uncertainty in real-time biomechanical data streams without relying on dense camera arrays.
gse_mapping: In GSE, situational reasoning transitions from pure dead-reckoning to aided localization upon detecting optical markers. This state-transition logic mitigates singularities during marker occlusion, ensuring continuous pose reconstruction by seamlessly blending inertial angular velocity integration with absolute trilateration coordinates.

The mathematical foundation of this patent rests on the duality between local differential kinematics and global integral geometry. Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) provide high-frequency angular velocity and acceleration vectors, which are integrated to yield orientation and position via dead-reckoning. However, this integration process inherently amplifies low-frequency sensor biases, leading to an unbounded drift in the absolute position estimate—a classic singularity in autonomous navigation. Conversely, optical tracking utilizes elementary trilateration to solve for the exact 3D coordinates of retro-reflective markers based on multi-camera triangulation. While this yields highly accurate, drift-free global positions, it is fundamentally constrained by line-of-sight requirements. The core operator derived here is the 'position aiding' mechanism: a hybrid state estimator that treats optical trilateration outputs as sparse but precise measurement updates to the continuous inertial state vector. Mathematically, this resembles an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) or a factor graph optimization where inertial odometry provides the temporal edges and optical hits provide absolute node constraints. The failure modes are dualistic: inertial systems fail due to accumulated integration error over time, whereas optical systems fail instantaneously upon marker occlusion. The sovereign primitive lies in the seamless transition between these regimes—using inertial data to bridge optical gaps and optical data to reset inertial drift, creating a robust, continuous pose estimation manifold suitable for complex sports environments.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theoretic perspective, the tracking system acts as an agent balancing exploration and exploitation of sensory inputs. It must dynamically weigh the reliability of the IMU against the availability of optical data. When occlusion occurs, the system's 'belief' shifts entirely to the inertial model, accepting higher uncertainty to maintain continuity. The opposing 'agent' is the chaotic physical environment causing occlusions, forcing the tracker into a reactive, probabilistic state rather than a deterministic one.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the optical reference frame is not perfectly aligned with the inertial magnetic or gravity-aligned frame. If the transformation matrix between the two domains contains significant rotational error, applying optical position aids will introduce catastrophic jumps in the inertial trajectory rather than correcting drift. Furthermore, if the frequency of optical updates drops below the Nyquist rate of the athlete's high-acceleration maneuvers, the inertial bridging may overshoot, causing phase lag artifacts.
